title: What Is D2C? Full Form, Business Model and Examples in India
summary: Learn the D2C full form, how the D2C business model works, its benefits and challenges, and examples of D2C brands in India, including boAt and Mamaearth.

The growth of India’s e-commerce industry over the last few years says a lot about the state of consumers and businesses. A deeper look shows that the industry is embracing digital-first D2C (Direct-to-Consumer) brands. These brands have reduced the role of middlemen. The D2C business model has seen an uptick in popularity among the general public.


With young startups challenging established giants in the Indian market, the D2C model continues to evolve. If you intend to enter this market, it is critical that you thoroughly understand the various aspects of D2C e-commerce. Let’s dig into the world of D2C.


### TL;DR


- D2C stands for Direct-to-Consumer. A D2C brand sells directly to customers through channels such as its website, app or owned stores.
- The model gives brands more control over customer relationships, pricing and the buying experience. Profitability depends on acquisition, fulfilment and service costs.
- Indian examples include boAt, Mamaearth and Wakefit. A brand can combine direct selling with marketplace and retail distribution.


##


D2C Full Form and D2C Brand Meaning


D2C, i.e. Direct-to-Consumer, is a business model where a brand sells its products directly to customers. The brand may manufacture its products or work with manufacturing partners. They can sell on their websites, mobile applications, owned retail stores or factory outlets. A D2C brand may also use e-commerce platforms like Amazon or Flipkart as additional channels. Businesses can also[sell on social media](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-links/) , for example, Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp.


All online ways of selling products via websites, apps or online shopping sites count as e-commerce.


In the D2C business, the brand manages the direct customer relationship. The D2C model reduces the need for wholesalers, third-party retailers, and other middlemen in the sales channel. This reduces the reliance on the third-party marketplace. Hence, D2C is a model where the brand reaches the consumers directly. Besides arranging manufacturing and shipping of their products, D2C companies also handle marketing, sales, and customer service.


D2C commerce enables brands to enter a market quickly with fewer traditional distribution constraints, although sales and fulfilment costs remain. With the rise of[e-commerce](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-gateway-for-ecommerce/) in the country, many businesses have taken advantage of the opportunity to cut out the middlemen and sell directly to their customers with the potential for a higher profit margin.


New brands can benefit from the D2C commerce model to jump on board while existing brands can broaden their reach by selling directly to customers. In either case, the core proposition of D2C brands revolves around providing consumers with direct product access.


##


How Does the D2C Business Model Work?


D2C business models work by connecting the brand directly to the end customer, giving it more control of marketing and sales strategies. The brand takes responsibility for its storefront, pricing, marketing, fulfilment and customer service. Partners can handle some of these functions.


##


Benefits of D2C eCommerce


- **Cost savings** : Cutting off middlemen can reduce the distribution and selling costs, potentially increasing the profit margins of the brand. The commission paid to other parties for supply and distribution also decreases. Furthermore, the availability of social media channels can contribute to lower costs per customer acquisition when used effectively. D2C brands must still account for marketing and fulfilment costs before assessing profitability.
- **Better Understanding of Consumer Behaviour** : As brands deal with customers directly, they can better gauge customer preferences through the customer database from past sales.
- **Command over the Value Chain:** If you make a product, you must first figure out how to get it into traditional markets. Since visiting every local store to place your products for sale is neither feasible nor economically viable, you would prefer something that breaks the usual pattern of doing business. You have more control over your own D2C e-commerce channels. The products manufactured can be branded better as the brand will be responsible for products reaching the target customer. You do not have to rely on retailers to establish long-term relations with your customers.
- **Brand Visibility:** Brand visibility can improve as customers see your products on your own website, with fewer competing products displayed alongside them. Due to the brand presence on various channels, customers can connect through various channels. This is an excellent opportunity to establish brand reach and build a large customer base.
- **Low Entry Barriers** : The supply chain of a product in a traditional distribution model passes through many hands. The manufacturer sells it to a distributor, who then sells it to a retailer, and finally, it reaches the customer. Between all of these stages, the success and reach of your products are determined by each middleman’s effort to push your products out for sale. They are less likely to be motivated to sell it further if they do not see good profit margins. D2C commerce enables brands to enter a market quickly with fewer traditional entry constraints such as access to distribution networks. Brands still have sales costs.


##


Challenges and Downsides of the D2C eCommerce Model


While there are many benefits of the D2C model, there are a few cons, like fierce competition from other brands and large retail chains that are already well-established in the market. Also, businesses now have to multitask in terms of sales, branding, marketing, logistics, and customer relationship teams alongside product development and manufacturing. Some of the downsides of D2C e-commerce and the challenges that they face are listed below.


### Fierce Competition with Established or Local Stores


It is challenging to battle these retailers who have a lot of experience in product sales and market reach. Not all retailers want a D2C brand selling similar products in their category online.


### Order Fulfilment


D2C brands frequently struggle to fulfill the orders received directly from their customers due to logistics and the time taken to ship their orders. Local retailers may offer immediate purchases, while some marketplaces provide faster delivery.


### Development and Maintenance of Technical Infrastructure


A proper technical infrastructure must be put in place and maintained for any D2C e-commerce business to succeed. This can be particularly challenging for new D2C businesses. The storefront needs reliable[payment integration](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/overview) , order management and customer support.


### High Marketing Costs


Although the D2C model allows you to broaden your horizons, implementing an effective marketing strategy requires significant investment.


##


D2C vs Traditional B2C Distribution


D2C is a form of B2C (Business-to-Consumer). The comparison below focuses on direct selling versus traditional distributor- and retailer-led distribution.


The table below compares the differences between selling products through a traditional distribution model and selling products through a D2C approach.


**Parameters** **Traditional B2C distribution** **D2C eCommerce model**


Supply chain model The product from the manufacturer reaches the wholesaler, distributor and retailers who then sell it to the consumer. The brand directly sells to the consumer through its own sales channels.


Costs involved Can be high due to the involvement of middlemen Intermediary margins may be lower as middlemen are eliminated, but acquisition and fulfilment costs remain


Profitability Net profit depends on margins, volume and operating costs Net profit depends on margins, acquisition costs, repeat purchases and operating costs


Access to consumer data Can lack access as various distribution stages are involved More direct access to customer data as the brand directly sells the products to consumers, subject to consent and privacy requirements


Online marketing impact Varies by channel and can be significant for online retailers Significant impact because it often relies on online traffic for sales


##


D2C Brand Examples in India


**Brand** **Products** **Example of direct selling**


boAt Personal audio products and wearables Customers can browse products and shop through the brand’s own online store.


Mamaearth Skin, hair and baby care products Customers can shop from the brand’s website.


Wakefit Mattresses, furniture and home products Customers can explore the brand and buy through its own online store.


These brands illustrate direct sales channels within a broader distribution strategy. Marketplace or retail sales can sit alongside D2C eCommerce.


##


FAQs about D2C Businesses


#### What Is the Difference Between D2C and B2C?


D2C is a model in which the brand directly sells to the consumer without wholesalers or third-party retailers. B2C is the broader category of businesses selling to consumers and includes D2C. Traditional B2C distribution follows the supply chain where the product from the manufacturer reaches the wholesaler, distributor, and retailers to sell to the consumer. B2C can also involve third-party marketplaces like e-commerce platforms.


#### Does D2C Complicate Business Processes for the Manufacturer?


The D2C model can complicate a business process for the manufacturer because the brand manages more functions directly. With potential for increased profit margins and direct control of the brand, the D2C model can offer long-term benefits. The first step is to choose the right platform, set up a shop, and plan marketing and branding. Working out logistics and customer service can help build the brand under the direct control of the manufacturer.
